title: A Debt for the Ghost
premise: Mara Marchetti, a fixer-interpreter who launders inconvenient truths for delegations that were never meant to succeed, discovers the safe house he's hidden in for two years is being sold online — complete with interior photos showing his face in a mirror. The listing is bait from Aldous Vey, the broker whose ledger of bought loyalties Mara once translated and then stole. To survive past the checkpoint shift change at dawn, Mara must trade back the one secret worth killing for: the name of the minister who ordered the delegation's massacre, a name Vey will sell to anyone — unless Mara gives it up first and burns his own leverage with it.
about_author: Jonah Nystrom is a former logistics coordinator for humanitarian missions who spent a decade watching negotiations fail politely across conference tables. He writes thrillers about the people paid to make failure sound like progress, and lives somewhere he refuses to list online.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Scrolling property sites at 3 a.m., Mara finds his own safe house for sale, every room photographed — including the mirror shot where his reflection lingers. A viewing is scheduled for tomorrow; the agent's name decodes to Vey's old cipher. The emotional beat is cold recognition: after two years as a ghost, someone has priced his life at market value.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Mara and Inspector Dana Kovač, who attends the open house hunting the interpreter who vanished mid-testimony. Mara enters disguised among buyers and realizes the photos weren't surveillance — they were an invitation, each room staged with an artifact from his stolen ledger. Kovač nearly catches him; instead she slips him her card. The beat is vertigo: hunter and hunted circling the same trap.

chapters.title: The Minister's Name
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, intercut with flashbacks to the massacre translation. Vey corners him in the house's cellar, offering survival in exchange for the minister's name — but reveals Kovač already has half the ledger, meaning the trade buys only hours. Mara must choose: sell the name and stay a ghost, or give it to Kovač and become a witness. The beat is the corrupting weight of power held too long.

chapters.title: Shift Change
chapters.summary: Split POV converging at the border checkpoint before dawn. Mara hands Kovač the name, accepting exposure, while Vey's buyers close in on both of them. Kovač uses her authority to hold the crossing just long enough; Vey is taken by his own creditors when the sale falls through. Mara walks through the checkpoint as himself for the first time in years. The beat is costly release: survival purchased with the self he was hiding.
